competitive_position.basis: Stated as a risk factor in the 10-K (P2); the competitive landscape is the company's own characterization.
competitive_position.claim: Criteo faces intense competition from large internet and technology companies with significantly larger resources, including Amazon Advertising, Google Search, YouTube, Chrome, Meta Platforms, and Apple Search Ads, and some large retailers may develop retail media advertising technologies in-house.
quotes: Certain internet and technology companies have significantly larger resources and capital than we do, and in many cases have advantageous competitive positions in popular products and services such as Amazon Advertising, Google Search, YouTube, Chrome, Meta Platforms, and Apple Search Ads, which they can use to their advantage.

Some large retailers, which could include our own clients, may develop retail media advertising technologies in-house, and may move some of their demand to a direct sales model such that they would do some of their own sales.

competitive_position.claim: As of September 30, 2026, Criteo's market capitalization fell below the aggregate carrying value of its reporting units, triggering an interim goodwill impairment test; no impairment was recorded but headroom was lower than in the prior annual assessment.
quotes: Due to the decline in the Company's stock price over recent months, which resulted in its market capitalization falling below the aggregate carrying value of its reporting units as of September 30, 2026, the Company performed an interim quantitative goodwill impairment test of the Performance Media and Retail Media reporting units as of that date.

Based on this assessment, the estimated fair values of both reporting units continued to exceed their respective carrying values, albeit with lower headroom compared to the previous annual impairment assessment. Accordingly, no goodwill impairment was recorded.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (SAM projections) and P4 (actual Q3 and 9M declines); the condition of stabilizing the two scope-change clients is stated in P4 and P7.
growth_thesis.claim: Retail media advertising spend is a growth driver with a SAM the company projects at $42 billion by 2026 and $50 billion by 2027 (excl. Amazon and China); for this to continue, the two Retail Media clients with previously communicated scope changes must not further reduce, and new retail partners must continue to onboard.
quotes: In Retail Media, excluding Amazon and China, our Serviceable Available Market ("SAM") is expected to reach approximately $42 billion in advertising spend by 2026 and $50 billion by 2027, reflecting a compound annual growth rate of about 20%.

Retail Media revenue decreased (23)%, or (22)% on a constant currency basis, to $52.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, reflecting the impact of previously communicated scope changes with two specific Retail Media clients, partially offset by continued strength in Retail Media onsite.

We expanded Retail Media adoption across approximately 4,700 brands and grew our retail network with new partners, including Notino in EMEA, El Puerto de Liverpool in Mexico, ONIGO in Japan, Adore Beauty in Australia, and PayU in India.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P7 (specific market rollout timeline) and P1 (industry trend framing); the margin-sustainability condition is inferred from P2's discussion of CPM-based pricing and fraud risk.
growth_thesis.claim: Cross-channel CTV expansion is a growth driver, with Performance CTV capabilities extending to Brazil and Mexico by year-end 2026 and to eight additional markets in 2027; for this to continue, advertisers must allocate performance-oriented budgets to CTV inventory in those new geographies at CPMs sufficient to sustain margin.
quotes: Criteo expands its Performance Connected TV capabilities beyond the U.S., starting with Brazil and Mexico by year-end 2026, followed by Canada, the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Australia, and select additional markets in 2027.

CTV has become the second fastest growing advertising channel after retail media. As audiences migrate from linear TV to streaming, marketers increasingly demand measurable, performance-oriented solutions for CTV that can be optimized like digital media.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (data scale figures) and P2 (regulatory risk); the condition that data access must be preserved is directly stated in P2's risk factor discussion.
growth_thesis.claim: The scale of Criteo's commerce data foundation—over 5 billion SKUs mapped, approximately 740 million daily active users via direct integrations, and more than 3 billion via social networks—is a growth driver; for it to continue, first-party data partnerships with retailers must be maintained and evolving privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, proposed EU GDPR amendments) must not materially restrict access to consented commerce data.
quotes: We curate one of the largest commerce data sets in the world, normalizing and mapping over 5 billion SKUs to brands, merchants, and transactions.
We reach approximately 740 million daily active users through direct integrations with thousands of media owner partners, and more than 3 billion daily active users through social media networks
In November 2025, the European Commission proposed a broad package of amendments to the GDPR intended to modernize and align the EU's data protection framework with other digital regulations.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (retention rate) and P4 (client mix, enterprise client spend reduction); the condition that large clients must stabilize is directly stated in P4.
growth_thesis.claim: High client retention (approximately 90% over the last three years) combined with new client additions is a growth driver; for organic growth to reaccelerate, the 6% of Q3 2026 revenue from new clients must expand, and several large enterprise clients whose spending has already reduced must not further cut budgets.
quotes: Each of the last three years, our average client retention rate remained approximately 90%, demonstrating the durability of our platform and relationships.
In the three months ended September 30, 2026, 94% of revenue came from existing clients while 6% came from new client additions.

Performance Media revenue decreased (9)%, or (8)% on a constant currency basis, to $371.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to soft performance in Commerce Growth and lower AdTech services, partially offset by an increase in our Supply Side Platform.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P7 (partnership, 89 countries) and P1 (industry framing); the condition of demonstrating advertiser ROI is inferred from P1's emphasis on measurable outcomes as the basis of Criteo's value proposition.
growth_thesis.claim: Advertising in AI-powered conversational search is an emerging growth driver, with Criteo as OpenAI's first advertising technology partner enabling brands to advertise on ChatGPT in 89 countries; for this to scale, advertisers must demonstrate measurable return on ad spend in the ChatGPT environment and the partnership must expand beyond its initial launch scope.
quotes: Criteo became OpenAI's first advertising technology partner in March 2026, enabling thousands of brands to advertise on ChatGPT; the offering is now available in 89 countries.

Agentic AI is emerging as a natural extension of how consumers discover and choose products online. AI-powered assistants and shopping agents are beginning to guide people through product discovery and decision-making in more personalized and efficient ways.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P7 (media spend figures) and P4 (macro disruption in specific verticals); the condition that budgets must not further deteriorate is directly stated in P4's macro discussion.
growth_thesis.claim: Total media spend through the platform is a growth driver, at $1.2 billion in Q3 2026 (up 9% YoY at constant currency) and $4.6 billion in the trailing 12 months; for this to continue, macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions must not further suppress advertising budgets, particularly in the Middle East and Travel verticals where disruption was already felt in 2026.
quotes: Criteo's media spend2 was $4.6 billion in the last 12 months and $1.2 billion in Q3 2026, up 9% year-over-year at constant currency3.

During 2026, geopolitical conditions and macroeconomic disruption have been increasingly volatile. In particular, we have experienced an impact on marketing budgets in the Middle East and in our Travel vertical.

risks.claim: Criteo faces ongoing and evolving privacy and AI regulatory exposure: the CNIL reduced a GDPR sanction to €40.0 million (paid in Q3 2023, under appeal), the European Commission proposed broad GDPR amendments in November 2025, and new California CCPA regulations take effect January 1, 2026.
quotes: In June 2023, the CNIL issued its decision, which retained alleged GDPR violations but reduced the financial sanction against Criteo from the original amount of €60.0 million ($65.0 million) to €40.0 million ($44.0 million). Criteo made the required sanction payment in the third quarter of 2023. The decision relates to past matters and does not include any obligation for Criteo to change its current practices. Criteo has appealed this decision before the Conseil d'Etat.
In November 2025, the European Commission proposed a broad package of amendments to the GDPR intended to modernize and align the EU's data protection framework with other digital regulations.

In September 2025, the California Privacy Protection Agency approved final regulations under the CCPA that significantly expand business obligations and consumer rights in California, including mandatory risk-assessments and annual cybersecurity audits for certain businesses; new rules governing the use of automated decision-making technology in connection with "significant decisions" about consumers; and enhanced disclosures, consent/opt-out mechanisms and documentation requirements in connection with consumer privacy rights. These new regulations will begin to take effect on January 1, 2026, with phased compliance deadlines.
